Document: Practice Direction 29
Part 2 of 2
==================================================
Where it appears inevitable the court may exercise its power to require a party as well as his legal representative to attend court at the hearing where such an order is to be sought. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 7.4] (7) The court will not postpone any other hearing without a very good reason, and for that purpose the failure of a party to comply on time with directions previously given will not be treated as a good reason. ## Pre-trial check lists (listing questionnaires)

## 8.1

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 8.1] (1) The pre-trial check list (listing questionnaire) will be in Form N170. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 8.1] (2) Unless it dispenses with pre-trial check lists and orders an early trial on a fixed date, the court will specify the date for filing completed pre-trial check lists when it fixes the trial date or trial period under rule 29.2(2). [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 8.1] (3) The date for filing the completed pre-trial check list will be not later than 8 weeks before the trial date or the start of the trial period. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 8.1] (4) The court will serve the pre-trial check lists on the parties at least 14 days before that date. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 8.1] (5) Although the rules do not require the parties to exchange copies of the check lists before they are filed they are encouraged to do so to avoid the court being given conflicting or incomplete information. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 8.1] (6) The file will be placed before a judge for his directions when all the check lists have been filed or when the time for filing them has expired and where a party has filed a checklist but another party has not done so. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 8.1] 8.2 The court’s general approach will be as set out in the following paragraphs. The court may however decide to make other orders, and in particular the court will take into account the steps, if any, of which it is aware which the parties have taken to prepare the case for trial. ## 8.3

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > 8.3] (1) Where no party files a pre-trial checklist the court will order that unless a completed pre-trial checklist is filed within 7 days from service of that order, the claim, defence and any counterclaim will be struck out without further order of the court. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 8.3] (2) Where a party files a pre-trial check list but another party (the defaulting party) does not do so, the court will fix a hearing under rule 29.6(4). Whether or not the defaulting party attends the hearing, the court will normally fix or confirm the trial date and make other orders about the steps to be taken to prepare the case for trial. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 8.3] 8.4 Where the court decides to hold a hearing under rule 29.6(4) the court will fix a date which is as early as possible and the parties will be given at least 3 days notice of the date. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > 8.3] 8.5 Where the court decides to hold a pre-trial review (whether or not this is in addition to a hearing under rule 29.6(4)) the court will give the parties at least 7 days notice of the date. ## Directions the court will give on listing

## 9.1

## Directions the court must give

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > Directions the court must give] The court must fix the trial date or week, give a time estimate and fix the place of trial. ## 9.2

## Other directions

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > Other directions] (1) The parties should seek to agree directions and may file an agreed order. The court may make an order in those terms or it may make a different order. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > Other directions] (2) Agreed directions should include provision about:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > Other directions] (a) evidence especially expert evidence,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > Other directions] (b) a trial timetable and time estimate,

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > Other directions] (c) the preparation of a trial bundle, and

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > Other directions] (d) any other matter needed to prepare the case for trial. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > Other directions] (3) The court will include such of these provisions as are appropriate in any order that it may make, whether or not the parties have filed agreed directions. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > Other directions] (4) Unless a direction doing so has been given before, a direction giving permission to use expert evidence will say whether it gives permission to use oral evidence or reports or both and will name the experts concerned. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > Other directions] 9.3 The principles set out in paragraph 6 of this practice direction about variation of directions applies equally to directions given at this stage. ## The trial

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > The trial] 10.1 The trial will normally take place at a Civil Trial Centre but it may be at another court if it is appropriate having regard to the needs of the parties and the availability of court resources. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > The trial] 10.2 The judge will generally have read the papers in the trial bundle and may dispense with an opening address. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > The trial] 10.3 The judge may confirm or vary any timetable given previously, or if none has been given set his own. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > The trial] 10.4 Attention is drawn to the provisions in Part 32 and the following parts of the Rules about evidence, and in particular:

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > The trial] (1) to rule 32.1 (court’s power to control evidence and to restrict cross-examination), and

[Part 35 Experts and assessors > The trial] (2) to rule 32.5(2) statements and reports to stand as evidence in chief. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > The trial] 10.5 In an appropriate case the judge may summarily assess costs in accordance with rule 44.6. Attention is drawn to the practice directions about costs and the steps the parties are required to take. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > The trial] 10.6 Once the trial of a multi-track claim has begun, the judge will normally sit on consecutive court days until it has been concluded. [Part 35 Experts and assessors > The trial] Updated: Monday, 30 January 2017
